newsitem.title: USA: New York Thruway rules out toll increases for now.
newsitem.headline: New York Thruway rules out toll increases for now.

text.p: New York State Thruway Authority said Thursday that drivers would not pay higher tolls for the "foreseeable future" due to the agency's program of cutting spending as well as the economy's rebound.
Further, the Authority said its new $191.7 million operating budget for 1997 trims spending by 10 percent from its original estimates.
Authority chairman Howard Steinberg said the Thruway's revenues rose $10 million over forecasts for 1996, mainly due to the improved economy.

Capital expenditures, which are predicted at $225 million to $250 million each year for the next six years, will be paid for with Thruway revenues, federal aid, and bonds. No details on Thruway's plans to sell debt were immediately available.

The chairman attributed much of the Thruway's focus on slashing costs to Gov. George Pataki. "Gov. Pataki strongly urged the Thruway Authority to re-evaluate the way we have done business to correct the deficiencies of the past administration and to find ways to control spending," he said in prepared remarks.
